answer: Because the timing is recorded against the prism challenge, the cipher audit can replay the ripple history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 147 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 28 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
